title: Rescue Rover Challenge
subtitle: Put the whole system together
description: One rover. One battery. Deliver supplies, locate a resident who needs help, avoid the flooded canal, and get home.
story: This is the full district. The canal has burst, a walkway has collapsed, and two blocks are still without supplies. Every team runs the same map with the same budget. The rover that comes home safely with the job done wins — not the one that drives fastest.
learningObjectives: Real engineering means balancing competing goals
Every component choice is a trade-off, not an upgrade
Systems fail at the joins between parts, not inside them
A reliable slow robot beats a fast unreliable one

objectives.description: Deliver at least one package to a supply station
Locate at least one resident needing help
Bonus: keep out of the flood water completely

failureConditions.message: The rover ran out of battery in the field and could not get home.
The recovery window closed before the rover returned.
The rover took too much damage to continue.

hints: Add a 'Battery below 25% → Return to base' rule near the TOP of your list. It is the difference between finishing and stranding the rover.
You cannot afford everything. Decide what this mission actually needs before you spend a single credit.
The efficient motor plus 60% power will get you much further than the high-torque motor at 100%.
Bonus objectives are worth attempting only if the required three are already safe.
reflectionQuestions: Which component did you cut to stay inside budget, and what did it cost you?
If you ran this mission again with the same budget, what would you build differently?
Which part of your system was the weakest link: the rover, the model, or the rules?
